message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc reported for the quarter ended 2026-07-31 revenue of 1.85 billion dollars, up 36.54 per cent on a year earlier, and earnings per share of 2.82 against an estimate of 2.16, a surprise of 30.56 per cent [D1]. Net income was 397 million dollars, up 107.85 per cent on a year earlier, with a gross margin of 65.87 per cent and a net margin of 21.51 per cent [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group contributed revenue of 1.35 billion dollars, up 43.09 per cent, and operating income of 458 million dollars, while the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group contributed revenue of 501 million dollars, up 21.60 per cent, and operating income of 155 million dollars [D1]. Total segment operating income of 613 million dollars was up 81.36 per cent [D1]. Guidance for the fourth fiscal quarter is revenue of 1.93 billion dollars to 1.95 billion dollars, which at the mid-point is 37 per cent growth, and earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 on 172 million diluted shares [D1].

That is the true part, and what the market argues about is whether it persists. The shares were marked down in the session after the release, on 2026-08-19, by 6.32 per cent despite the 30.56 per cent earnings surprise, so the reported beat did not settle the question [D1]. On one side, demand is described as far exceeding the ability to supply and the pipeline is said to keep growing strongly [D3]. On the other, management itself calls supply chain the governor of near-term revenue and warns that the supply situation is likely to be nonlinear, with supply governing the conversion of demand into revenue for the next several quarters [D3]. A further part of the argument is the quality of the beat, since management said one-time tariff impacts artificially pulled up fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat, which raises the comparison bar [D3]. Into that argument come a forward price to earnings multiple of 20.66 and a trailing multiple of 45.89, set against a sequential revenue step of 7.51 per cent on the quarter before [D1].

The plan is therefore to judge the next report against the guidance the company gave rather than against the beat just delivered [D1]. That means fourth quarter revenue inside the 1.93 billion dollar to 1.95 billion dollar range and earnings per share inside 3.34 to 3.40 [D1]. It means watching whether gross margin holds near 65.87 per cent and net margin near 21.51 per cent, since the tariff benefit does not repeat [D3]. It means watching whether supply rather than demand determines conversion, because management says supply will remain the governor and the situation is likely to be nonlinear [D3]. It means watching the Communications Solutions Group, at 1.35 billion dollars of revenue and 43.09 per cent growth, and the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group, at 501 million dollars and 21.60 per cent growth, for signs that the mix has narrowed to a single driver [D1].

The conditions are explicit on both sides. If revenue lands below 1.93 billion dollars or earnings per share below 3.34, the bear case is confirmed [D1]. If both land inside the range with margins intact and the segment momentum of the third quarter still visible, the bull case is [D1]. Everything between those two outcomes is a question about supply, and that is the question the next report has to answer [D3].
